description: Measured Search geometry ratchet (WP1.5b/S3), using real registered jf-sv3-window captures. Ceilings, overlap counterparts and required selectors must be visible with positive width and height. Legacy names identify retained camera recipes, not an old component mount.
captureState: Built UI, isolated headless Chromium, deterministic HTTP fixtures. Search captures run in dark and light; forced-colors hero/dock/palette and 760px narrow result/composer states are explicit. Each changed bound was measured on 2026-10-28. agent-budget owns an open loopback SSE fixture for the real waiting decision, closed with its context.
constraintKinds: Element size/reading bounds, positive visible required selectors, overlap relations, named non-scrollers, min/max scrollable-region bands, viewport bottom bounds and visible-text/status assertions. Any absentSelectors assertion needs a positive visible requiredSelectors witness in the same step. Hidden, zero-size, missing or incomplete constrained geometry is an error, never a clean ceiling or overlap.
occlusionNote: Search reader crowding is measured at 1250x800 with an actual result and reader plus three visible toasts. Sources/composer overlap is measured at max scroll. Retired: chat-spine-single/multi, because Search has no minimap; three-zone 55/45 shares, because Search owns a different layout; wide full-bleed banner and escalation-strip assertions, because Search keeps composer, prose and notice together at its current 48rem reading measure. Surviving budgets, activity, message, notice, reader and composer checks below use Search controls. The activity expansion floor remains essential: a positive 43px collapsed card must fail a 100px expanded floor (217px measured open).
rolesNote: Tempdoc 816 — the INLINE axis joins the block axis in this register, and it joins it with a different KIND of invariant, deliberately (816 §2b). Height is zero-sum inside a viewport, so its invariant is a budget over the sum (814's share floors / chrome ceilings above). Width is handed out top-down and rows stack, so the unconsidered default is greedy 100% and the right invariant is a PER-ELEMENT functional bound in CONTENT units: an element's width claim must be justified by its function, not by available space. Hence `roles` below: each role cites the function that produces its number, element rows reference a role via `inlineSizeRole` instead of repeating it, and the number is resolved at measure time against the bound element's own rendered font (`chPx`) rather than being stored as px. THE SAME NUMBER RENDERS: each role's `token` names the CSS custom property in modules/ui-web/src/styles/tokens.css that applies it, and the gate fails on drift between the two — one authority renders AND judges (§4a.3). ANTI-VACUITY, inherited from this register's doctrine: a ceiling alone is satisfied by an element that failed to render, so a role-bound row must also carry a floor (the role's `minInlineSizeCh` or the row's own `minWidthPx`), and a selector missing from the capture stays an ERROR. ADOPTION IS BY EXPLICIT ROW, one surface at a time (§4a's adoption path) — 'every text-bearing element declares a role' is the named end-state, NOT the current rule; `pane` is declared `documentational` because the existing minWidthPx/minShareOfSelector rows already cover panes physically and force-migrating them would buy nothing.

prose.why: Line-length legibility — the reading measure. External authorities cluster below this (USWDS ~75ch, Tailwind 65ch, WCAG 1.4.8 AAA <= 80ch); 88ch is the value this surface already shipped and is kept for the first instance so exactly one thing changes, with narrowing judged live (816 §5's open owner decision).

text-entry.why: Max: what you type you immediately re-read, so an entry field takes the reading measure. Min: a typical query unwrapped (~30ch) — below that the field stops being usable for its own content, which is the floor that keeps the ceiling non-vacuous.

notice.why: A notice's content box is its own text at reading measure and no more; its BACKGROUND may still bleed edge to edge (816 §2's full-bleed-chrome role: the chrome is full-width, the content is content-sized). No `minInlineSizeCh` — a notice's floor is its longest word plus its action control, which is content-dependent, so rows binding this role carry their own `minWidthPx` floor instead.

pane.why: A space-sharing pane's function genuinely IS 'share of workspace', so its bounds belong to the container-% family (`minWidthPx` floors and `minShareOfSelector`), NOT to content units — 816 §2b's crossover case. Declared for vocabulary completeness; the `.conversation` / `.document-pane` / `jf-task-list` rows above already express it physically, so nothing is force-migrated.

steps.$comment: WP1.5b measured Search: Submitted Ask with compact degradation; measured notice 36px, question 47px. Both remain bounded.
WP1.5b measured Search: 1250x800: Search main 790px, reader 360px; three 288x50 toasts begin below the 52px Search topbar. Reading/reader floors replace old pane/zone allocation.

Tempdoc 859 §B — the FIRST occlusion row on the Search window, and the first sv3 step that runs under `--fixtures` at all. §B moved the composer out of document flow and onto a floating `div.dock` over the transcript's one scroller; the whole correctness claim is that the scroller's padding + scroll-padding grow by the dock's MEASURED height, so 'scrolled to the end' means 'the last line is above the glass'. That is a RELATION between two rects and no per-element size budget can express it. Captured at 1280x800 with the `sv3-sources` fixtures variant (a thread record whose last assistant message carries populated `attributes.citations`, plus deliberately long answers so the transcript overflows), Sources disclosure OPEN, scrolled to max — the only position where the assertion means anything, since at rest the last element is nowhere near the dock. NON-VACUITY, per this register's own occlusionNote: two 0x0 rects never intersect, so BOTH selectors carry a `minHeightPx` floor; without them the overlap row would report clean precisely when neither element rendered. The floors are deliberate minima, not measured widths — the dock's resting docked height is the composer's glass box plus its inset (~104-140px in source geometry, which is what bounds how far the floor can be raised) and the three-source panel is taller than one row. CALIBRATED 2026-08-25 against an ACTUAL `--fixtures` capture of this step (the state this gate enforces — the earlier landing note's numbers were never captured, and the 859 live-leg audit reported the same three values from the running app): Sources panel h=237 at y=380, docked band h=155 at y=617, so the dock's bottom edge is 772 in the 800px viewport. `sv3-turn-citations.minHeightPx` moves 40 -> 120 and `sv3-dock.minHeightPx` 60 -> 120 — an effective floor of 118 after tolerance, still under the source-geometry minimum above, so a real dock cannot trip it while a stub instead of a real disclosure now fails rather than reporting clean. `sv3-dock.maxBottomPx` moves 800 -> 780: at 800 the bound WAS the capture viewport and could never fail; 780 sits 8px under the measurement and outside the 2px tolerance, making it an assertion about the dock rather than a restatement of the window size. On the overlap row: the panel's bottom (617) and the dock's top (617) sit at an EXACT 0px boundary in this state, where the live app shows a 12px inset gap because the last element under the dock differs. That is not fragility — the gate requires more than tolerancePx of REAL intersection on both axes, so a flush edge is clean by construction and only a genuine cover-up goes red. Verified: `jseval ui-proportion-gate` exit 0, all six rows of this step ok. It is still not part of hosted CI, so re-seat these at the next capture if the fixture state moves.

WP1.1 S1.12 — Search mode's result list stays reachable beside the floating composer at a narrow width with a long list. Captured at 760x720 with the `sv3-results` fixtures variant (24 hits), scrolled to the end; the step itself fails if the list did not overflow and reach its end, so the overlap row cannot pass on a list that never scrolled. NON-VACUITY per this register's occlusionNote: both selectors carry a `minHeightPx` floor. CALIBRATED against the first `--fixtures` capture: card h=1947 with its bottom at 581, dock h=99 at y=593 (bottom 692), scroller delta 1499 — a 12px gap between the last row and the glass. The card floor (600) is far under the measurement but over anything a short list or a stub renders; `maxBottomPx` is 700, not the 720 viewport, so it asserts something about the dock.
WP1.5b measured Search: Recorded Delegate tool card collapsed at 43px; composer shell 75px. Retires the three-zone share and keeps bounded activity.
WP1.5b measured Search: Detailed notice 76px vs compact 36px; 64px floor discriminates expansion. Composer shell stays 75px.
WP1.5b measured Search: 760x600: dock 99px, bottom 572px. 580px bottom cap leaves usable viewport space.

Actual main Search ownership witness, idle and without plugin or override. The visible compact authority banner owns the degraded fact; the global Service degraded chip must yield. Required compact banner plus the unchanged42px bound prevents empty-success captures. Canonical stale status/settings bytes are preserved: Indexing status unconfirmed may still appear twice, outside this bounded sentinel and registered same-string singleton claim.
WP1.5b measured Search: Search Sources disclosure replaces the old docked evidence rail. Three real source cards; panel 297px, one overflowing transcript scroller, no panel scroller.
WP1.5b measured Search: Tool-card expansion: 217px vs 43px collapsed. Floor 100px keeps expansion distinct even when hidden body nodes exist. Body and activity must also be visible.
WP1.5b measured Search: 1920x900: Search prose/composer/notice 768px, textarea 744px, composer height 75px. Current 48rem measure replaces old text-entry 88ch and full-bleed banner bounds.
Real Delegate budget decision waiting on open SSE, not a terminal/error approximation. Prompt 239px high and facts 18px. Actions must be visible before axe.
